short: Moved the court to Nara in 710 and had the Kojiki presented to her in 712.
full:
Genmei took the throne in 707 on the death of her son, Emperor Monmu, whose own heir was a child of six. She was the fourth woman to reign in her own right, and like several of them she held the position as a stopgap within the ruling family rather than as a claimant in her own line.

In 710 she moved the capital from Fujiwara-kyō to Heijō-kyō, on the site of modern Nara, laying it out on a grid modelled on Tang Chang'an. Earlier courts had shifted with each reign; this one stayed for eighty-four years, and the period takes its name from it. The Kojiki, the oldest surviving Japanese book, was presented to her in 712, and in 713 she ordered the provinces to compile the geographical records known as fudoki. She abdicated in 715 in favour of her daughter, who reigned as Empress Genshō — the only direct succession from one empress regnant to another.
